name: Question 7
problem:
The velocity $v$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
v(t)=⟨\frac{1}{2t},\,\frac{1}{3t}⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $r=⟨1,2⟩$ when $t=1,$ calculate the position of $P$ at time $t=e.$ Do not round the answers.

$r(e)=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$
worked_solution:
To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨\frac{1}{2t},\,\frac{1}{3t}⟩\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int \frac{1}{2t}\,\text{d}t,\int \frac{1}{3t}\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t+{C}_{1},\,\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡t+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $r(1)=⟨1,2⟩.$ Substituting $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(1) & =⟨\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)+{C}_{1},\,\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨1,2⟩ & =⟨{C}_{1},\,{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have ${C}_{1}=1$ and ${C}_{2}=2.$ Therefore, the position vector at time $t$ is given by

$$
r(t)=⟨\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t+1,\,\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡t+2⟩.
$$

To find the position vector at time $t=e,$ we substitute $t=e$ into the above, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(e) & =⟨\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)+1,\,\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)+2⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2}(1)+1,\frac{1}{3}(1)+2⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{2},\frac{7}{3}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that r(1)=⟨1,2⟩. Substituting t=1, we get

r(1)=⟨12ln⁡(1)+C1,13ln⁡(1)+C2⟩⟨1,2⟩=⟨C1,C2⟩,

so we must have C1=1 and C2=2. Therefore, the position vector at time t is given by

r(t)=⟨12ln⁡t+1,13ln⁡t+2⟩.

To find the position vector at time t=e, we substitute t=e into the above, and we get

r(e)=⟨12ln⁡(e)+1,13ln⁡(e)+2⟩=⟨12(1)+1,13(1)+2⟩=⟨32,73⟩.
